chunks: Abū Muḥammad al-Qāsim ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, raised it from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim, who said:

We were with al-Riḍā عليه السلام in Marw. We gathered in the congregational mosque on Friday at the beginning of our arrival, and they discussed the matter of the Imamate and mentioned the extent of people’s disagreement concerning it. So I entered upon my master عليه السلام and informed him of the people’s disputation about it.

He عليه السلام smiled and then said: O ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, the people have become ignorant and have been deceived by their opinions. Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not take the soul of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله until He completed the religion for him and sent down to him the Qur’an, in which is the clarification of everything. In it He clarified the halal, the haram, the limits, the rulings, and all that people need in full.
We have not neglected anything in the Book.
And He revealed during the Farewell Hajj, which was at the end of his life صلى الله عليه وآله:
Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My blessing upon you, and approved Islam for you as a religion.

And the matter of the Imamate is part of the completion of the religion. He صلى الله عليه وآله did not pass on until he clarified for his community the landmarks of their religion, made clear to them their path, left them upon the straight course of the path of truth, and established for them ʿAlī عليه السلام as a standard and an Imam. He left nothing needed by the community except that he clarified it. So whoever claims that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not complete His religion has rejected the Book of Allah, and whoever rejects the Book of Allah is a disbeliever in it.

Do they know the worth of the Imamate and its place in the community such that their choosing in it should be valid? Surely the Imamate is too exalted in worth, too great in station, too high in place, too fortified in aspect, and too deep in depth for people to reach it by their intellects, attain it by their opinions, or appoint an Imam by their own choice.

Surely the Imamate is that with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singled out Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl عليه السلام after prophethood and intimate friendship, as a third rank and a virtue by which He honored him and magnified his mention, so He said:
Indeed, I am making you an Imam for the people.
So the Friend عليه السلام said, rejoicing in it: And from my offspring? Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.

Thus this verse nullified the imamate of every wrongdoer until the Day of Resurrection, and it came to be among the elect. Then Allah, Exalted, honored him by placing it in his offspring, the people of purity and selection, so He said:

And We bestowed upon him Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb as an additional gift, and each We made righteous. And We made them Imams guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishing of salat, and the giving of zakat, and they were worshippers of Us.

So it continued in his offspring, inherited by one from another, generation after generation, until Allah, Exalted, caused the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله to inherit it. So He, Majestic and Exalted, said:
Surely the nearest of people to Ibrāhīm are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the guardian of the believers.

Thus it became exclusively his, and he صلى الله عليه وآله vested it in ʿAlī عليه السلام by the command of Allah, Exalted, in accordance with the form that Allah had ordained. Then it came to be in his offspring, the purified ones to whom Allah gave knowledge and faith, by His saying:
And those who were given knowledge and faith said: You have indeed remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

So it is specifically in the descendants of ʿAlī عليه السلام until the Day of Resurrection, since there is no prophet after Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله. Then from where are these ignorant ones choosing? Surely the Imamate is the station of the prophets and the inheritance of the وصيّs. Surely the Imamate is the succession of Allah and the succession of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, the station of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and the inheritance of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام.

Surely the Imamate is the reins of the religion, the order of the Muslims, the rectification of the world, and the honor of the believers. Surely the Imamate is the growing foundation of Islam and its lofty branch. Through the Imam comes the completion of salat, zakat, sawm, hajj, and jihad; the proper administration of fayʾ and charities; the execution of legal penalties and rulings; and the protection of the frontiers and borders.

The Imam makes lawful the halal of Allah, prohibits the haram of Allah, establishes the limits of Allah, defends the religion of Allah, and calls to the path of his Lord with wisdom, good exhortation, and conclusive proof.

The Imam is like the rising sun whose light envelops the world, while it remains on the horizon beyond the reach of hands and sights. The Imam is the radiant full moon, the shining lamp, the brilliant light, and the guiding star in the depths of darkness, across cities, deserts, and the surging seas.

The Imam is sweet water in thirst, the guide to guidance, and the savior from ruin. The Imam is the fire upon a height, warmth for the one who seeks heat from it, and the guide amidst perils; whoever separates from him is destroyed.
The Imam is the rain-bearing cloud, the pouring rain, the shining sun, the sheltering sky, the broad earth, the abundant spring, the pool, and the garden.
The Imam is the intimate companion, the compassionate father, the full brother, the kind mother to a small child, and the refuge of the servants in overwhelming calamity.
The Imam is Allah’s trustee among His creation, His proof over His servants, His vicegerent in His lands, the caller to Allah, and the defender of the sanctities of Allah.

The Imam is purified from sins and cleared of faults, distinguished by knowledge, marked by forbearance, the order of religion, the honor of the Muslims, the rage of the hypocrites, and the destruction of the disbelievers.

The Imam is unique in his age: none comes near him, no scholar equals him, no substitute is found for him, and he has no likeness or peer. He is specially endowed with all excellence without his seeking it or acquiring it; rather, it is a distinction from the Bestowing Giver.

So who is there that can attain knowledge of the Imam, or who can possibly choose him? Far, far from it! Intellects have gone astray, understandings have wandered, minds are bewildered, eyes have grown dim, the great have diminished, the wise are confused, the forbearing fall short, the orators are constrained, the intelligent have become ignorant, the poets are exhausted, the men of letters are incapable, and the eloquent are unable to describe even one aspect of his affair or one virtue among his virtues, and they confess incapacity and deficiency.

And how can he be fully described, or his reality characterized, or anything of his affair understood, or anyone found who can take his place and suffice as he suffices? No, how and from where? He is like the star, far beyond the reach of those who would grasp it and the description of those who would describe it. So where is choice in relation to this? Where are intellects in relation to this? And where can the like of this be found? Do you think that this can exist outside the family of the Messenger Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله? By Allah, their own souls have lied to them, and falsehood has filled them with vain hopes.

They have climbed to a difficult and slippery ascent from which their feet slip down to the lowest depth. They sought to establish the Imam with bewildered, failing, deficient intellects and misguided opinions, and they gained from it nothing but remoteness. May Allah destroy them—how are they turned away! They attempted a difficult matter, spoke falsehood, strayed far astray, and fell into confusion when they abandoned the Imam knowingly. Satan adorned their deeds for them and turned them away from the path while they had insight.
They turned away from the choice of Allah, the choice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and his Ahl al-Bayt, to their own choice, while the Qur’an calls out to them:
And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they do not have the choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate.
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair.
—the verse. And He said:

What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Or do you have a book in which you study, that you may have in it whatever you choose? Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection that you shall indeed have whatever you decide? Ask them which of them will guarantee that. Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.
And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon hearts?
Or has Allah set a seal upon their hearts, so they do not understand?

Or did they say, We hear, while they do not hear? Surely the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf, the dumb, those who do not reason. If Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would still have turned away while refusing.
Or did they say: We hear and we disobey?
Rather, it is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of tremendous grace.

So how can they have any role in choosing the Imam, while the Imam is knowledgeable and not ignorant, a shepherd who does not shrink back, the mine of holiness, purity, devotion, asceticism, knowledge, and worship; singled out by the supplication of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله and from the lineage of the purified, chaste Lady; with no blemish in his lineage, and no man of noble ancestry can approach him in the house of Quraysh, the summit of Hāshim, the progeny of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, and the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?

He is the nobility of the noble and the branch of ʿAbd Manāf, ever-growing in knowledge, perfect in forbearance, bearing the burden of the Imamate, knowledgeable in governance, obedience to him being obligatory, established in the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sincere toward the servants of Allah, and a guardian of the religion of Allah.

Surely the Prophets and the Imams, may Allah’s blessings be upon them, are granted success by Allah, and He gives them from the storehouses of His knowledge and wisdom what He does not give to others. Thus their knowledge is above the knowledge of the people of their time, as in His saying, Exalted is He:
Is then one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who does not guide unless he is guided? So what is the matter with you? How do you judge?
And His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He:
And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given abundant good.
And His saying regarding Ṭālūt:
Surely Allah has chosen him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body; and Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and Allah is all-encompassing, knowing.
And He said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله:
He sent down upon you the Book and the wisdom, and taught you what you did not know, and the grace of Allah upon you has been immense.
And He said regarding the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt of His Prophet, his family, and his offspring, may Allah’s blessings be upon them:

Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His grace? Indeed, We gave the family of Ibrāhīm the Book and the wisdom, and We gave them a mighty kingdom. So among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it; and sufficient is Jahannam as a blazing fire.

Surely when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chooses a servant for the affairs of His servants, He expands his breast for that, deposits in his heart springs of wisdom, and inspires him with knowledge by inspiration. Thereafter he is never unable to answer, nor confused away from what is correct. Thus he is maʿṣūm, supported, granted success, and rightly directed, secure from sins, slips, and stumbles. Allah singles him out with that so that he may be His proof over His servants and His witness over His creation. And that is the grace of Allah—He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of tremendous grace.

So are they able to find the like of this, that they may choose him? Or can their chosen one possess this description, that they may advance him? By the House of Allah, they have transgressed against the truth, and they have cast the Book of Allah behind their backs as though they did not know. In the Book of Allah are guidance and healing, yet they cast it aside and followed their desires. So Allah censured them, detested them, and brought them to ruin, and He, Majestic and Exalted, said:
And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
And He said:
So destruction be upon them, and He has made their deeds go astray.
And He said:
Greatly hateful it is in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant tyrant.
And may Allah bless the Prophet Muḥammad and his family, and grant abundant peace.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: the Prophet’s family, identified here as the locus of Imamate
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةَ: the divinely appointed office of Imam and religious leadership
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated leader who guides and safeguards the religion
key_terms.الْحَرَامَ: what Allah has made forbidden in religion
key_terms.الْحَلَالَ: what Allah has made permissible in religion
key_terms.الْحِكْمَةَ: divinely granted wisdom enabling true judgment and guidance
key_terms.حُجَّتُهُ: His proof; a divine authority established over creation
key_terms.مَعْصُومٌ: protected from sin, error, and deviation

ai.seo_question: Why, according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, can the Imam not be chosen by the people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Riḍā عليه السلام presents the Imamate as a divinely appointed office that completes religion and cannot be determined by human choice. It describes the Imam as the inheritor of prophetic authority, uniquely endowed with divine knowledge, purity, and guidance, and supports these claims through a sustained appeal to Qur’anic verses.
